title: Every crossing check is measured by the inspector; transitions only compares
intention: Every check the crossing runs is done by build_inspector: nine functions in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py return each lane's expected and actual, and the gates in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py only wrap those entries, compare them and kick back, measuring nothing themselves.
why: Outline 19.14.1 (Akien, 2026-10-27): 'the inspector does all the checks. so there is no need for more checks.' Today nine lanes in transitions.py read tickets, journals, validations and repos themselves, so a crossing's verdict has two mouths: the inspector's sieves and the gate's own reads. Moving the checks gives one, and child 4's certificate then certifies what the inspector found rather than what the gate decided.
traces_to: Akien 2026-10-27, outline 19.14.1 and 19.14.4: the inspector does all the checks; entry gates only kick back. Parent ticket e41a94da3fd0 (child 2). Law 4 (the rule is an AST tooth). RULE 1 (base asks build_inspector through the inspector module, which its charter's public_interface declares).
how: Move each check's measuring body from transitions.py into a crossing_ function in inspector.py that returns its checks as dicts (D1, D2), with its helpers (D3). Rosters stay in transitions and are passed in (D4). The rules grammar moves to workflow_grammar (D5, D6), and watchme_spec stops importing transitions (D7). _require_demo and _quorum_gate split the same way (D8, D9). The proof is pre-written (D10); the regression net is D11.
falsifier: Green when cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_the_crossing_compares_what_the_inspector_found.py passes all five teeth under PROVES {'66ee1ffc1ec7': {'1'..'5'}} (D10) and the D11 regression net stays green: (1) none of the nine transitions functions calls a world reader or builds a lane with expected=; (2) each imports exactly one crossing_ function from build_inspector.inspector; (3) on world-free fixtures each record entry carries the inspector's source and equals the crossing_ function's checks; (4) workflow_grammar defines the seven rules helpers and transitions' names are the same objects; (5) the inspector defines the nine crossing_ functions and its import closure reaches neither transitions.py, gate_probes.py nor bus_client/. Wrong intent if Akien means the gate should stop composing lanes and read one inspector verdict instead.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> FIXME -> BUILDME -> [PROVEME:waiting] -> PROVED

decisions.text: The inspector does every check; the gate only wraps, compares and kicks back (outline 19.14.1). Each check now in transitions.py moves into a function in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py that returns its CHECKS: a list of dicts {identity, expected, actual, values}, one per lane, in the order the gate journals them, nesting included (a lane whose input failed is absent, as today). It never returns []. transitions.py turns each check into a proof-record entry through one new helper, _inspected(code, sieve_name, checks), which calls _lane(identity, expected=..., actual=..., code=code, source='build_inspector.inspector.' + sieve_name, **values). _lane gains a keyword-only source= that defaults to today's 'transitions.' + function name. Every entry keeps its identity, location, code, expected, actual and values; only source changes, and it now names the function that owns the rule. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-28 'keep going without stopping until you need me. we're all pre-approved thru proved.'

The nine inspector functions, with these exact names and signatures, in one new section of inspector.py headed THE CROSSING'S CHECKS (ticket 66ee1ffc1ec7), placed after proved_answers_the_chart: crossing_emission(obj, ticket); crossing_rules(wf, target, class_def); crossing_named_ticket(target, ticket, *, history_path, roster); crossing_fixme(ticket, history_path=None); crossing_demo(ticket); crossing_clearance(target, journal_extra, *, history_path, roster); crossing_proof_named(ticket, journal_extra); crossing_durability(ticket, *, history_path=None); crossing_quorum(validation_path, class_def). Each body is the measuring body of its transitions counterpart, moved verbatim except that _lane(...) becomes a plain dict and _find_ticket/_tf._TICKETS become ticket_file.find_ticket / ticket_file._TICKETS read at call time (632edb992aa3 tooth 6: _TICKETS is the one patch point). CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-28 'keep going without stopping until you need me. we're all pre-approved thru proved.'

These helpers move with them, verbatim, into the same section of inspector.py and leave transitions.py: _latest_kick_back, _when, _named_on, _dead_names, _repo_toplevel, _durability_roots. _dead_names resolves relative names against the inspector's own _REPO_ROOT (the same directory transitions' _REPO_ROOT names). transitions.py keeps none of them unless a proof outside the build names one; measured at build by grep over every proofs/ dir, and a hit is bound back by name rather than edited. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-28 'keep going without stopping until you need me. we're all pre-approved thru proved.'

The two rosters stay in transitions.py (_EXEMPT_ROSTER, _CLEARANCE_EXEMPT_ROSTER) and are passed as roster= at call time. They are the gate's policy, not a measurement, and test_transitions rebinds transitions._EXEMPT_ROSTER, so reading it at call time keeps those teeth meaningful. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-28 'keep going without stopping until you need me. we're all pre-approved thru proved.'

The grammar the rules check needs moves from transitions.py into cairn/tools/base/workflow_grammar.py, verbatim: is_disposition, _registered_workflow, _conform, canon_target, resolve_target, _REST_DISPOSITIONS and legal_targets. transitions.py imports them back by the same names, so they are the same objects and cross.py, test_watchme_vocabulary, test_v2_migration and test_system_word keep working. workflow_grammar.py gains one import, 'from cairn.tools.system_word.system_word import canon', a module whose own top-level imports are the standard library. load_class_def stays in transitions.py: it reads a file and is called by emit, not by a check. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-28 'keep going without stopping until you need me. we're all pre-approved thru proved.'

The light-modules proof (cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_light_modules_keep_the_crossing_off_the_inspector_path.py) tooth 1 widens its allowed non-stdlib imports for workflow_grammar.py from DiagnosticBase alone to DiagnosticBase and cairn.tools.system_word.system_word, and adds system_word.py to the files whose own top-level imports must be stdlib. Its PROVES key stays 632edb992aa3; the tooth's point (the grammar loads nothing that posts) is unchanged. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-28 'keep going without stopping until you need me. we're all pre-approved thru proved.'

cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py's three call-time imports 'from cairn.tools.base.transitions import parse_workflow' (lines 89, 96, 331) become 'from cairn.tools.base.workflow_grammar import parse_workflow'. Measured 2026-10-28 with import_sieve.reaches: watchme_spec's closure is 90 files including transitions, gate_probes and bus_client; that edge is the only one, so the inspector can call watchme_spec without reaching the crossing. armed_error's importlib load of the probe berth stays: it is a dynamic import the walk cannot see, the residue CLAUDE.md names under ticket sole-path-sees-subprocess-and-dynamic-import, and this ticket does not widen it. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-28 'keep going without stopping until you need me. we're all pre-approved thru proved.'

_require_demo splits. crossing_demo(ticket) returns one check (demo_gate_ticket_readable when no ticket file resolves, demo_gate_binding_check when the ticket has no demo flag) or two (demo_gate_flag_bound, demo_validation_exists). The demo_validation_exists values gain last_date and last_method (the latest green demo validation's date and method, None when there is none), because the clean note reads them and transitions may not read the validation itself. transitions returns (None, record) when record[0]['identity'] is one of the two non-firing lanes, raises DemoGateRed with the same message when demo_validation_exists mismatches, and otherwise returns the same note built from those two values. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-28 'keep going without stopping until you need me. we're all pre-approved thru proved.'

_quorum_gate keeps its note, _red and BUILD_GATE.run in transitions; only the record comes from crossing_quorum(validation_path, class_def). inspect_emission, inspect_rules, inspect_named_ticket, inspect_fixme, inspect_clearance, inspect_proof_named and inspect_durability keep their names, signatures and return values, and each becomes two statements: import its crossing_ function at call time, return _inspected(code, name, checks). The refusals and notes that read record values (_emission_gate, validate_transition, _require_named_ticket, _require_clearance, _clearance_refusal, _proof_named_gate, the exit gate's durability ledger) are unchanged. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-28 'keep going without stopping until you need me. we're all pre-approved thru proved.'

The proof is cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_the_crossing_compares_what_the_inspector_found.py, written red-first and committed before BUILDME; the builder only runs it. PROVES {'66ee1ffc1ec7': {'1','2','3','4','5'}}. (1) AST over transitions.py: none of the nine functions (inspect_emission, inspect_rules, inspect_named_ticket, inspect_fixme, _require_demo, inspect_clearance, inspect_proof_named, inspect_durability, _quorum_gate) calls a world reader from this set: open, read_text, read_bytes, loads, load, is_file, exists, glob, iterdir, stat, _find_ticket, find_ticket, standing, read_validations, validations_path_for_artifact, repo_truth, proven_by_since_buildme, spec_for, armed_error, watchme_spec_error, read_history; and none calls _lane with an expected= keyword. (2) Each of the nine imports exactly one name from cairn.machines.build_inspector.inspector, that name starts with crossing_, and inspector.py defines it. (3) Behaviour on fixtures needing no world: for rules (a legal and an illegal edge), emission (no ticket), named_ticket (no ticket), fixme (an unresolvable ticket), clearance (no cleared_by), proof_named (a ticket with no crossings), durability (a tempdir), quorum (no validation path) and demo (an unresolvable ticket), every entry transitions returns carries source 'build_inspector.inspector.crossing_<x>' and equals, on identity, expected, actual and values, what the crossing_ function returns for the same arguments. (4) workflow_grammar defines the seven rules helpers and transitions' names for them are the same objects. (5) import_sieve.reaches from cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py contains neither transitions.py, nor gate_probes.py, nor any file under cairn/tools/bus_client/. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-28 'keep going without stopping until you need me. we're all pre-approved thru proved.'

Regression net, all green before BUILDME and after the build, any red a FIXME: cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_transitions.py, test_emission_gate.py, test_a_fixme_answer_binds_to_its_kick_back.py, test_proveme_names_its_proof.py, test_a_dead_proof_name_is_refused_at_proveme.py, test_the_stones_are_pushed.py, test_proveme_entry_needs_a_clean_tree.py, test_watchme_vocabulary.py, test_v2_migration.py, test_light_modules_keep_the_crossing_off_the_inspector_path.py; cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/proofs/test_clearance.py; cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_inspector_nexus.py; cairn/tools/system_word/proofs/test_system_word.py. A baseline of which are green at HEAD is taken first; a proof red at HEAD is recorded as such, never counted against the build. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-28 'keep going without stopping until you need me. we're all pre-approved thru proved.'

Out of scope: inspect_entry, inspect_exit, inspect_clean_tree and inspect_build, which already compose build_inspector; emit's bus post (32f500e517d7); certificates on the crossing (child 4); moving gates and inspectors under CodeMother (outline Q#31). The rules check now imports the inspector on every journaled crossing: measured 2026-10-28, importing inspector after transitions costs 9 ms, and emit is the only caller of validate_transition, so it is paid once per crossing (an event, not a poll).
